section_name: Methodological Limits of Evaluating on Fitting Observations

candidates.title: A survey of cross-validation procedures for model selection
candidates.reason: Comprehensive review examining how evaluating prediction rules on fitting data introduces systematic downward bias, surveying cross-validation frameworks designed to obtain honest out-of-sample predictive performance estimates.

candidates.title: How Biased is the Apparent Error Rate of a Prediction Rule?
candidates.reason: Foundational paper that defines and quantifies optimism, demonstrating why the apparent error rate computed on the fitting observations systematically underestimates true prediction error due to the covariance between observations and fitted values.

candidates.title: The Estimation of Prediction Error: Covariance Penalties and Cross-Validation
candidates.reason: Establishes the mathematical connection between in-sample apparent error, covariance penalties, and out-of-sample prediction error, showing why adjustments calculated and evaluated on the same observations require explicit correction.

candidates.title: To Explain or to Predict?
candidates.reason: Influential methodological analysis delineating in-sample explanatory fit from out-of-sample predictive validity, documenting why optimizing or assessing models on fitting observations has limited implications for generalization.

candidates.title: Cross-Validatory Choice and Assessment of Statistical Predictions
candidates.reason: Seminal work formalizing the distinction between assessing a prediction prescription on fitting data versus independent validation, establishing the protocol for honest predictive evaluation.

candidates.title: What You See May Not Be What You Get: A Brief, Nontechnical Introduction to Overfitting in Regression-Type Models
candidates.reason: Pedagogical review detailing how evaluating fitted parameters on the identical observations used for estimation produces an illusion of predictive accuracy that fails to generalize.

candidates.title: The Problem of Overfitting
candidates.reason: Broad methodological survey explaining why goodness-of-fit metrics computed on training samples overestimate predictive performance when models capitalize on sample-specific characteristics.

candidates.title: Points of Significance: Model selection and overfitting
candidates.reason: Concise methodological review illustrating the divergence between training error on fitting observations and out-of-sample test error across varying degrees of model adjustment.

candidates.title: Choosing Prediction Over Explanation in Psychology: Lessons From Machine Learning
candidates.reason: Methodological review addressing the widespread conflation of in-sample statistical fit with genuine predictive capability, emphasizing the requirement of out-of-sample evaluation protocols.

candidates.title: Multivariable prognostic models: issues in developing models, evaluating assumptions and adequacy, and measuring and reducing errors
candidates.reason: Foundational guide on model development and validation, detailing why evaluating performance on development data yields overly optimistic metrics and outlining procedures for measuring optimism.

candidates.title: Internal validation of predictive models: efficiency of some procedures for logistic regression analysis
candidates.reason: Methodological review comparing validation procedures, quantifying the extent of apparent-performance optimism when models are assessed on the same observations used for derivation.

candidates.title: Cross-Validation Methods
candidates.reason: Expository review of single-sample fit statistics versus sample-reuse assessment methods, detailing why evaluating predictive accuracy on fitting observations is inherently optimistic.

candidates.title: Statistical Modeling: The Two Cultures
candidates.reason: Landmark paper contrasting goodness-of-fit evaluation on training observations with empirical predictive verification on unseen observations.

candidates.title: Cross-validation failure: Small sample sizes lead to large error bars
candidates.reason: Methodological review highlighting the vulnerability and high variance of evaluating model performance in small-sample regimes, contextualizing the hazards of fitting and assessing on restricted observation sets.
